subject: Feature enablement: streaming + tool-calls + structured JSON schema — passoff questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie@medicore.com>, Greg Torres <greg.torres@medicore.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Feature enablement: streaming + tool-calls + structured JSON schema — passoff questions

Hi Sophie / Greg —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our handshake, I'm attaching a short mutual action plan and the initial JSON schema draft for the streaming payload (streaming_json_schema_v1.json) plus a short doc with example tool-call payloads (toolcall_examples.md). Before Rafael and Monica pick this up for the implementation sprint, a few clarifying questions from our side so we can finalize acceptance criteria: 

1) Acceptance criteria for structured outputs: do you require a single top-level JSON object per message (preferred), or can you accept newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for higher throughput?
2) Tool calling: which of your internal services need synchronous tool calls (blocking) vs. async callbacks? We need the list so we can configure function invocation timeouts and retry policies.
3) Streaming behavior: what's your target end-to-end latency SLA for first token (ms) vs. total response time? This informs batching and KV cache sizing.
4) Schema evolution: do you have an internal contract process we should mirror (e.g., version bump + changelog + migration window)?

Requested next steps: please reply inline with the answers above and confirm a preferred date for a short 30-minute schema walk-through (we're proposing Wed 1/17 at 10am PT). Rafael will lead the implementation plan and Monica will own QA acceptance and runbooks.

Attachments: medicore_enablement_MAP_2028-01.xlsx (spreadsheet), streaming_json_schema_v1.json (application/json), toolcall_examples.md (text)

From: Sophie Lane <sophie@medicore.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greg Torres <greg.torres@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature enablement: streaming + tool-calls + structured JSON schema — passoff questions

Marissa —

Thanks for the materials. Quick answers inline below: 

> 1) Single top-level JSON object per message or NDJSON?
We prefer a single top-level JSON object. Our downstream validators assume a single payload per message.

> 2) Synchronous vs async tool calls?
Two services need synchronous tool calling: (a) patient-match service (blocking, <3s required) and (b) insurance-lookup (blocking, <2s). All others can be async with an acknowledgement callback.

> 3) Target latency SLA?
Target first token ~120ms, total response under 2s for the common path. We understand there will be variance on long outputs.

> 4) Schema evolution process?
We have a lightweight contract process: bump minor version for additive fields, major version for breaking changes, and a two-week migration window (we can coordinate on a rollout doc).

We can do Wed 1/17 10am PT — Greg and I will join. Please add a calendar invite. Also: one constraint — our security team requires that streaming payloads do not include raw PHI values in the top-level output; redaction or tokenization is preferable. We'll share a short redaction checklist before the call.

— Sophie
Product Manager, Medicore Health

Thanks Sophie — very helpful. Quick notes and follow-ups before the Wed schema walkthrough: 

• Schema and streaming format: we'll lock to a single top-level JSON object per message. We'll add an envelope field ("meta") that can indicate redacted fields and tokenization method so your validators can still rely on a consistent shape.

• Tool-call topology: Rafael will configure two sync call routes with low timeouts + fast-fail behavior to avoid queue buildup. For each sync call we'll emit a status object in the structured output so you can trace the call result. Example snippet (from toolcall_examples.md):

{
  "action": "insurance_lookup",
  "params": {"policy_number": "<redacted>"},
  "result": {"status": "ok", "coverage": {...}}
}

• Streaming performance: to meet ~120ms first-token we recommend the following defaults for your pilot environment: batch window 8–12ms, max batch size 8 (for gpus with ~32GB), KV cache warmup on common prefixes, and prefix caching for repeat prompts. We'll bring measured numbers to the Wed call.

• Acceptance criteria (proposed):
  - Structured output matches streaming_json_schema_v1.json with schema validation passing for 98% of production test cases.
  - Synchronous tool-call latency p95 < 2.5s in pilot traffic.
  - No top-level PHI in outputs unless explicitly whitelisted via the redaction envelope.

Action items before Wed:
  1) Greg/Sophie: confirm redaction checklist and share any sample payloads you want validated (share to the Drive link).
  2) Medicore: grant a temporary read-only API key for Rafael to run a smoke test against a staging endpoint (we'll request scoped keys).
  3) Redwood: Rafael + Monica will prepare a short slide with test harness and QA checklist.

I'll send the calendar invite for Wed 1/17 10am PT and include a short agenda.

— Marissa
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference

All —

Thanks for confirming. Short status update and commitments from our side: 

1) I've scheduled the schema walk-through for Wed 1/17 10am PT and attached a short runbook slide (I put a copy in the Drive folder). Agenda: schema shape, redaction envelope, tool-call contract examples, test harness plan.

2) I'll request a scoped, read-only staging API key from our security team today; Monica will run the QA harness against the key on Friday and share results early next week.

3) On synchronous calls: we'll implement a hard timeout of 2.5s and a circuit-breaker after 5 consecutive failures for the patient-match route. For insurance-lookup we'll keep a retry=1 with exponential backoff and log the raw request/response in a trace object (redacted) for post-mortem.

4) Deliverables by next checkpoint (2028-01-24):
  - Implementation PR + test suite (Rafael)
  - QA acceptance checklist and runbook (Monica)
  - Finalized streaming_json_schema_v1.json -> v1.1 with the "meta.redaction" envelope (Marissa to coordinate)

If Sophie / Greg can drop sample payloads into the Drive folder today that will let us finish the PR faster. Otherwise we'll use synthetic samples and follow up.

Thanks everyone — excited to get this live.

— Rafael
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
